anatomy.intro: Paired fleshy leaves carry two different textures: marginal teeth and raised face tubercles.

parts.function: The compact triangular to rhomboid blade stores water.
parts.label: Thick leaf blade

parts.function: Short pale projections line the leaf edge; they are not cactus areoles.
parts.label: Marginal teeth

parts.function: Blunt whitish bumps rise above the flatter pale dots on the upper surface.
parts.label: Raised tubercles

parts.function: New paired leaves expand from the short shoot's center.
parts.label: Central leaf pair

flowers.text: The flowers are yellow. Because F. tigrina also flowers yellow, the raised leaf tubercles and shorter marginal teeth are more useful comparison features than bloom color alone.

growth.note: The published description allows anything from one raised tubercle to a densely bumpy upper surface, so bump coverage varies naturally.

stages.text: The central shoot develops another opposed pair.
stages.title: Add paired leaves

stages.text: Several thick leaves make the low, jaw-like rosette.
stages.title: Form a compact crown

stages.text: Additional shoots can broaden a mature plant beyond a single crown.
stages.title: Develop a clump

habitat.text: Faucaria tuberculosa comes from the Fort Beaufort area of South Africa’s Cape Provinces. This subtropical succulent stays close to the ground, growing as a single compact crown or a cluster. Its thick leaves present two conspicuous textures: pale teeth along the edges and blunt raised bumps across the upper faces.

lookalikes.name: Faucaria tigrina
lookalikes.text: Tigrina has conspicuous soft, thread-tipped marginal teeth and white spotting. Tuberculosa's raised blunt bumps on the leaf faces and shorter teeth support the current probable identification.

mature.text: Plants can remain solitary or develop clumps. Each rosette typically carries 4–8 leaves, with individual blades about 15–20 mm long and wide.
